title: Session affinity credits aggregator with failure-safe reconciliation
text:
Session affinity credits aggregator with failure-safe reconciliation

description:
Problem: Short-lived sessions and multi-route requests cause fractional token assignments and orphan credits when downstream services fail or replay. This ticket implements a durable aggregation layer that collects per-session token deltas, maintains session affinity across route fanouts, and exposes an eventually-consistent reconciliation path to ensure fair crediting and conservative billing.

Goals:
- Preserve per-session affinity metadata across gateway fanout so multi-route requests attribute tokens to the original session owner reliably.
- Provide a failure-safe aggregation buffer that can accept out-of-order events, de-duplicate repeated deliveries, and produce idempotent token delta outputs for downstream billing jobs.
- Emit reconciliation snapshots and annotations to allow retroactive corrections with confidence scoring rather than immediate hard adjustments.
- Keep tail latency on the hot path below 50ms added per request and ensure the aggregation worker scales linearly with throughput.

Approach:
1) Capture lightweight session affinity headers at ingress and propagate via request envelope.
2) Introduce an append-only shardable event buffer (s3-backed segments + local RocksDB index) to persist token deltas with monotonic session sequence numbers.
3) Build an aggregation worker set that consumes buffered segments, performs idempotent aggregation keyed by session_id+route_version, and writes aggregated deltas to the canonical metering topic for downstream billing and chargeback.
4) Add a reconciliation pass that compares aggregated deltas to final settled ledger entries and emits corrective patches to a correction topic with an attached confidence score and reason codes.
5) Instrument end-to-end traces and expose a per-session reconciliation dashboard to support SRE and Customer Support investigations.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change pricing or billing UI UX. Complex rate ladder recalculation is left for a follow-up.

Acceptance criteria:
- Aggregation worker passes synthetic load test at 10k reqs/s with 99th percentile per-request overhead <50ms.
- No more than 0.1% of sessions exhibit duplicate double-credit after a 24h reconcile window in the staging dataset.
- Reconciliation patches include an audit reason and confidence score and are consumable by the existing billing pipeline without schema changes.
- End-to-end test coverage for out-of-order ingestion, duplicate delivery, and late arrival rewrites.

comments:
2026-02-26 Miguel Ortega: Spike complete — prototype uses RocksDB index + streaming segments. Found edge-case where session sequence wraps on long-lived connections; added 64-bit monotonic sequence plan.
2026-03-02 PM Review - Lila Park: Confirmed customer-impact assumptions for sessions with cross-route fanout. Suggested adding confidence bands to reconciliation patches; added to ACs.
2026-03-04 Design feedback - Jonah Reed: Recommended using an explicit session envelope schema to avoid shadow headers. Link to design sketch: https://drive.google.com/designs/redwood/session-affinity-agg
2026-03-06 Eng update: Implemented buffer segment writer and local indexing. Running local integration tests against kafka-mock.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12488
2026-03-09 QA: Found a race when a segment compaction coincides with an in-flight aggregation job; added advisory lock and backoff strategy.
2026-03-10 Miguel Ortega: Canary deploying aggregation worker to staging cluster with 50% traffic. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood-inference.internal/dashboards/recon-agg-canary

notes:
Consider future optimization: KV cache for per-session small aggregates to reduce write amplification.
If confidence scoring shows low reliability for certain routes, we will fallback to conservative billing (credit back) and flag customer impact.
Follow-up ticket: add UI for ops to trigger manual reconciliation and dry-run patches (PM to create).
